- When sentiment is consistently negative (≥15 days), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >15% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1.5x prior peak for 3–7 days.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 40), model overreacts; apply downward bias of 2–5% per day until reversal.
- When sentiment flips from negative to positive (e.g., +1.00 after -1.00), model delays correction; adjust forecast 2–3 days ahead to align with sentiment shift.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent highs; use 10–15 day moving average as baseline for smoothing out 30d forecast.
- If true outcome shows “drop after spike” pattern (e.g., spike → 3–5 day decline), model fails to anticipate; reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 days post-spike.
